scope: Mosaic-only Luna conversational UX fork; ElevenLabs only; always-on voice; the mosaic is a hollow stone sphere (flat medallion at /?flat); a dropped PDF is swallowed through a crack in the shell; published as a static site on GitHub Pages

automatedTests.alsoRunBy: the GitHub Actions workflow, before every publish

ui.browser: Headless Brave (Chromium) driven over the DevTools protocol, at 2x device scale
ui.onlyInteractiveControl: The mosaic, and only while Luna is not live: pressing it retries. There is no stop or mute.
ui.voiceCanvasChanges: Stones gain colour glazes while live. The person's voice is a tide of turquoise glaze travelling inward from the rim in rings while each course turns as a rigid ring (a vortex); Luna's is warm glaze travelling outward. Course rotation and rim drift are the original.
statesSeen: turquoise tide from the rim and vortex twist during the spoken question

frameCostMs.note: time inside each animation frame while speech was drawn

piecesOnly.rule: Every effect is an individual stone travelling, turning or taking a glaze. No scale, filter, blend or overlay.
piecesOnly.notExercised: The pointer tilt from the original renderer foreshortens the stones under the cursor by up to 5% to show them tipping. No pointer was present in this run.

sphere.address: / (the default). The flat medallion is at /?flat
sphere.renderer: WebGL2. Two real objects, the mortar's cells (one rigid slab to each place, with an underside and cut sides, so the shell is hollow and can break) and the stones (the sphere's own plus the nine of a document's sheet), drawn twice a frame: the light's depth view, then the picture. Depth test and face culling only; no blending, no image files, nothing drawn after the picture.
sphere.motion: mechanical: twelve ticks a second, parts travel between fixed stops; stones lift clear, turn over and seat to show another stone; rings index by whole places with their mortar; rings stand up as pistons in whole notches
seenLiveOnFinalBuild: grey limestone in relief on rough mortar while connecting
stones turning over to colour from the pole outward on going live
blue and yellow stone at rest
sphere.voiceMechanismsCheckedBy: replaying a recorded real session (state, level and both spectra) through the motion: up to 698 of 3,596 stones turned to Luna's stone while she spoke and 1,678 to green while the person spoke, returning afterwards; and by 16 motion tests

footOfPage.visibleText: none, at rest, while dragging, and with a document in hand (checked by reading every visible text node in the lower part of the page)
footOfPage.names: a document's or a chapter's name shows for about three seconds where Luna's words go: when the document is read, when a chapter is chosen, and while its stone is pointed at
footOfPage.filePicker: pressing the mosaic twice opened the file picker, with a mouse and with touch emulation
footOfPage.keyboard: Tab reached a hidden "Add a PDF" control, which became visible only while focused

liveCheck.outputCaption: Seventeen times nineteen is three hundred twenty-three.

limits: Physical microphone acoustics were not tested. The visual gate and scale were calibrated on a synthetic voice and adapt to the speaker, but have not been seen with a real voice or room noise.
Resting after a silent 30-minute session, and reconnecting after a spoken one, are covered by unit tests of the policy only; no session was run to the provider's time limit.
A real network loss was not reproduced: DevTools offline emulation did not end the WebRTC session. The retry path was exercised by failing the token request instead.
The agent re-engages after roughly ten seconds of silence ('Are you still there?'). That is agent configuration, unchanged here.
The provider conversation has current-session memory; hiding the tab or reconnecting starts a new conversation.
Starting audio with no click was verified in Chromium only, and depends on the microphone already being allowed. Safari and Firefox were not run.
The sphere's cell shell and the swallow were seen only in headless Brave (software WebGL) on one machine. Its frame cost has not been measured.
Safari and Firefox were not run, on desktop or phone. No real phone was used: phone checks are Chromium's touch emulation.

studyMaterial.seenInHeadlessBrave: a generated 7-page PDF dragged from the page's lower right towards the sphere at 1024x768: a sheet of nine pale stones followed the pointer; the shell cracked open towards it, showing a dark hollow inside, wider as it came nearer; on the drop the stones went in and the pieces shut; a band of pale stones crossed the sphere; the document's name appeared; three chapter stones answered to pointing and pressing
studyMaterial.phone: 390x844 with touch emulation: two taps opened the picker, the chosen PDF was swallowed from the foot of the page, tapping a chapter stone chose it; no sideways scroll
studyMaterial.byTest: pieces of shell are carried only by unit turns and shifts; stones in a piece keep their distances; rings do not turn while the shell is open; all nine sheet stones end inside the shell before it shuts; no stone shows the page before the shell shuts, hundreds do at once after, none is left; chapter stones stand in order

contextMessagesSent.onChoosing: that chapter's text, up to 15,000 characters in three messages

notChecked: a real textbook or lecture PDF
a real drag from Finder with the operating system's own drag image over the page
frame cost of the cell shell on a phone or an integrated GPU: it draws about 400,000 triangles twice a frame
the flat medallion, which keeps its older intake and now has no chapter list beside it

staticSite.how: npm run build:pages: relative paths, the content policy in the page, a public ElevenLabs agent named by its ID. No API key in the site, the repository or the workflow (tests/static-site.test.mjs; a scan of every committed file for the two key values in .env found none).
staticSite.hostnameList: Names aboufama.github.io. ElevenLabs enforced it for its WebSocket transport (another origin was refused with code 3000) but not for WebRTC, which the page uses: with 'require an origin' on, every WebRTC conversation from the published page itself was refused, so it is off. Any site with the agent ID can therefore hold a WebRTC conversation; the limits above bound the cost.
staticSite.account: Creator plan, usage-based billing off when checked on 2026-10-03: an exhausted month stops Luna everywhere until the credits reset.
